summary: All 29 mutants of test-strategy sections 7.2 and 7.3 plus m-x and m-cd were run in scratch roots; 28 are killed and 1 (m-cd) confirms the known F207 residual. The 21 doctor.sh mutants of section 7.2, the 127-case test mutant, and all 5 record mutants of section 7.3 died on first run. Mutant m-x (grep -qF instead of grep -qxF in the drift match) survived the 24-case suite, as Review B N3 predicted; the new case drift_match_requires_whole_line kills it and passes on the real doctor.sh. Mutant m-cd (a step 4 command whose cd fails) gives exit 1, and the gate records a boundary verdict and exits 0, which confirms F207; no case can pin it without a change of doctor.sh, so it is a PM finding, not a missed mutant. The new case is committed in 5293392b8, and PROJECT_TESTS exits 0.
nonblocking_findings: F207 pin check (concurs with Review A r2 and Review B r2): m-cd confirms the mechanism. In a scratch root without packages/architecture-enforcement, the cd fails, the subshell gives exit 1, and measure/doctor.sh prints 'ARCHITECTURE: step 4 exits 1; the owner of the remaining drift is architecture_ci_input_pin_20261110' and exits 0. No case of tests/orchestrator_doctor_gate.sh can pin this today, because pinning needs doctor.sh to distinguish a failed cd from a CLI boundary exit 1, and that is a change of doctor.sh plus a spec amendment. This is not counted as a missed mutant.

handoff: QUESTION FOR THE PM (via the orchestrator), with my default. F207 cannot be pinned by a test case today: a failed cd or an uncaught Node exception gives exit 1, and measure/doctor.sh records it as a boundary verdict and exits 0 (m-cd proves it). Pinning needs doctor.sh to tell a failed cd from a CLI exit 1, for example by sending an exit 1 with no boundary report text down the tool-failure path (Review A option 2). Option 1: accept the residual with the caveat sentence of Review A r2 (default). Option 2: harden doctor.sh in a later task with a spec amendment; the hardened rule is testable, and the harness of tests/orchestrator_doctor_gate.sh can pin it with a stub exit 1 that prints no boundary report. DEFAULT if no answer: option 1. m-x is closed: the new case drift_match_requires_whole_line kills it and passes on the real doctor.sh (commit 5293392b8). No missed mutant remains. Any later change of measure/doctor.sh or the record invalidates the kills and reruns this gate.
